questions.stem: An algorithm is a c-approximation for a minimisation problem iff:
choices: ALG(I) <= c * OPT(I) for every instance I
ALG(I) >= c * OPT(I) for every I
ALG runs in O(c * n) time
questions.explanation: c-approximation: worst-case ratio bound. Smaller c is better; c >= 1 for minimisation.

questions.stem: What is the approximation ratio of the matching-based VC algorithm (pick uncovered edge, add both endpoints)?
questions.explanation: 2-approx: |C| = 2|M|, and any VC has |S| >= |M|, so |C| <= 2|OPT|.

questions.stem: What is the lower bound on OPT used in the VC 2-approximation proof?
choices: Size of the maximal matching produced by the algorithm
questions.explanation: Any VC must include at least one endpoint per matched edge, so |OPT| >= |M|.

questions.stem: Weighted Vertex Cover by pricing method achieves what ratio?
questions.explanation: Pricing / LP rounding: w(C) <= 2 * sum p_e <= 2 * w(OPT).

questions.stem: In the pricing method, a vertex is 'tight' when:
choices: Sum of p_e on incident edges equals its weight w_i
questions.explanation: Tight = its weight budget is fully allocated to incident edge prices. The algorithm outputs all tight vertices.

questions.stem: Greedy Set Cover's approximation ratio is:
questions.explanation: Greedy picks the most cost-effective set each step; charging gives an H_n approximation. Tight unless P = NP.

questions.stem: Greedy Set Cover picks at each step the set with:
questions.explanation: Cost-effectiveness = cost / |newly covered|. This local choice gives the H_n bound.

questions.stem: Metric TSP has a 2-approximation via:
choices: MST, doubling edges, Eulerian tour, shortcut by triangle inequality
questions.explanation: MST <= OPT; doubling gives Eulerian; shortcutting (triangle inequality) gives a Hamilton tour of weight <= 2 MST <= 2 OPT.

questions.stem: List scheduling on identical machines yields what approximation ratio for makespan?
questions.explanation: Assigning each job to the least-loaded machine gives a 2-approx; LPT improves to 4/3 (or 3/2 generally).

questions.stem: The competitive ratio of an online algorithm compares it to:
questions.explanation: Competitive ratio = ALG(I) / OPT(I), where OPT has full input in advance.

questions.stem: What is the competitive ratio of the optimal deterministic ski-rental algorithm?
questions.explanation: Rent until you've spent B; then buy. Worst case ALG = 2B, OPT = B.

questions.stem: Why is OPT not directly computable in an approximation analysis?
choices: Computing OPT is the NP-hard problem we are trying to bypass
questions.explanation: If OPT were computable in polynomial time we wouldn't need an approximation. The proof uses a structural lower bound instead.

questions.stem: The 'fairness inequality' in the pricing method states:
choices: sum of p_e >= w(S) for any vertex cover S
sum of p_e <= w(S) for any vertex cover S
questions.explanation: Each S must pay for every edge at least once via the tightness of its vertices, so w(S) >= sum p_e. This bounds OPT from below.

questions.stem: Which algorithm achieves a 3/2-approximation for metric TSP?
choices: Christofides (MST + min matching on odd-degree vertices)
questions.explanation: Christofides uses an MST plus a minimum-weight perfect matching on odd-degree vertices to obtain a 3/2-approx for metric TSP.

questions.stem: Why is the VC 2-approximation considered 'tight'?
choices: Algorithmic constant cannot be improved by any polynomial algorithm (under UGC)
questions.explanation: Khot's Unique Games Conjecture implies no polynomial algorithm achieves ratio better than 2; a disjoint-edge family achieves the bound.

questions.stem: Greedy Set Cover ratio H_n is tight in what sense?
choices: There is an explicit instance family approaching H_n
questions.explanation: Classic instance families (e.g., 'geometrically nested sets') approach the H_n bound. Hardness results show no o(ln n) algorithm exists under P != NP.

questions.stem: Which problem does NOT have a constant-factor approximation in this unit?
questions.explanation: Set Cover's best polynomial approximation is H_n = log n. The others have constant factor algorithms (2, 3/2, 2).

questions.stem: Which is a STRUCTURAL lower bound on OPT for VC?
questions.explanation: VC must hit every matching edge; any matching's size is a valid lower bound on |OPT|.

questions.stem: An online algorithm 'commits irrevocably' means:
choices: Decisions cannot be revoked once made
questions.explanation: Online's defining constraint: as input arrives, the algorithm chooses; later input cannot retroactively change earlier choices.

questions.stem: Why is greedy Set Cover analysis a 'charging argument'?
choices: Each element pays a share of its set's cost; summing charges gives ALG, and bounding charges by 1/(remaining covered) gives the H_n term
questions.explanation: Charging elements with the per-element cost at the time they get covered totals ALG; the harmonic bound on per-element charges gives H_n * OPT.

questions.stem: LPT (Longest Processing Time first) for makespan on identical machines:
questions.explanation: LPT sorts jobs longest-first, then list-schedules. Tighter analysis gives 4/3 (or 3/2 worst case).

questions.stem: The optimal competitive ratio for online paging with cache size k against arbitrary requests is:
questions.explanation: LRU is k-competitive; no deterministic online algorithm does better against the worst-case request sequence.

questions.stem: Why does a constant offset in the image-segmentation reduction not affect the ratio guarantee in Week 12-style approximation analysis?
choices: Constants do not appear here; image segmentation is solved exactly via min-cut
questions.explanation: Image segmentation has a polynomial exact algorithm via min-cut. No approximation needed.

questions.stem: An algorithm with competitive ratio strictly greater than 1 means:
choices: It always loses to OPT by a factor
It can be worse than OPT but by a bounded factor on any input
questions.explanation: Competitive ratio c > 1 says ALG <= c * OPT; on some inputs the gap is achieved, but it never exceeds c.

questions.stem: Which is the cleanest way to PROVE tightness of a c-approximation?
choices: Construct an instance family where ALG / OPT approaches c
questions.explanation: Tightness needs an adversarial input that matches the worst-case ratio; for VC's 2-approx, disjoint K_2's suffice.
